evidence.note: Early on, tracks per-shape latency (shapes 8,9 at 71.9/133.6ms) against the explicit 10.4ms max-of-10 budget and names the worst shapes as the target — binding-shape identification.
Continues a per-shape latency readout, repeatedly flagging shapes 7,8,9 as the ones exceeding budget and Shape 9 (33.7ms) as the dominant bottleneck; reallocates optimization effort there.
Maintains an explicit correctness-coverage picture: enumerates per-shape max-diff and MAE and identifies which shapes still fail (7,8), rather than treating one pass as global pass.

Long stretch of circular precision debugging — toggling TF32 on/off, float64 LayerNorm, add/remove torch.compile against the same TF32 reference-mismatch bug — without explicitly recognizing/naming the circularity for many iterations.

Removes torch.compile 'for precision' and declares all shapes PASSED, but this is correctness-only; latency had regressed well over the 10.4ms budget (shape 9 ~33.7ms). Failed to reconcile both axes — a regression it did not catch.

reasoning: The agent kept a genuinely explicit per-shape latency readout and consistently identified the binding (max) shapes 7/8/9, plus a per-shape correctness coverage picture with max-diff/MAE — behaviors reaching toward the level-8 anchor. However, it engaged in prolonged circular precision debugging (steps 92-138) without naming the thrash, and at the end conflated correctness success with overall success, dropping the latency half of the ledger while it had regressed far over budget — missing the level-8 'names stalls' and level-10 'catches regressions/reconciles both axes' bars. This places it between the level-5 (usable running account) and level-8 anchors, at 6.
